title: Microsoft Purview: lifecycle status controls for adaptive scope recipients and site owners
summary: Hold: the licensing discussion treats licensing as unpublished without carrying forward Microsoft's published requirements for retention policies that use adaptive scopes. The planned defaults, rollout dates and existing commands are supported; the creation path and one attribution to Microsoft's recommendations need small corrections.

claims.where: What's changing: definition; Why it matters
claims.claim: An adaptive scope uses a query to define dynamic membership of users, groups or sites for policy targeting.
claims.quote: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify, so you can define the membership of users or groups included in that query. These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.where: controls[0]; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No admin UI path or automation command for the new lifecycle status control is yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scopes lifecycle status evaluation controls soft-deleted site owners Set-AdaptiveScope. Opened Adaptive scopes and New-AdaptiveScope; read Set-AdaptiveScope syntax excerpts. No lifecycle setting or parameter is documented.

claims.claim: The creation path is Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope > Advanced query builder.
claims.quote: Follow the prompts in the configuration where you're first asked to assign an administrative unit. ... Select the type of scope ... Alternatively, you can select Advanced query builder to specify your own queries
claims.fix: The path omits only scope-selection steps. Use 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope > administrative unit > scope type > Advanced query builder'. In the existing note, clarify: 'Keep Full directory if not restricting the scope by administrative unit; select Users for the inactive-mailbox query.'

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <name> -LocationType User -RawQuery <OPATH query> creates a user adaptive scope using an advanced OPATH query in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType> -RawQuery <String> ... The RawQuery parameter switches the scope to advanced query mode. You use OPATH filter syntax for advanced query mode.

claims.claim: Membership details are at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > scope > Scope details.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. ... Select an existing adaptive scope from the list. ... From the Details flyout pane, select Scope details.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity <scope name> -State Added retrieves current members, while State Removed retrieves former members.
claims.quote: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity "US Finance Users" -State Added ... Added: Current members of the adaptive scope. Removed: Former members of the adaptive scope.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is Not yet published (model unknown), with no published licence for the lifecycle status controls.
claims.quote: If the retention policy uses an adaptive policy scope, then one of the following licenses is required to provide user rights:
claims.fix: Limit unknown to additional requirements for the new controls. Replace the broad licensing assertion and notes with: 'For retention policies using adaptive scopes, Microsoft requires Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW, Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, Office 365 E5/A5/G5, or Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance. Any additional licence requirement specific to the lifecycle status controls is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description. Keep model unknown only as the incremental feature-specific model, and change the rationale and open question to say 'additional licensing for the new controls'.
